svg.aria-label: How does a learned proposal become justified physical action?

a.xlink:title: The point where an admitted command becomes physical work in the world.
Delivered physical work cannot be recalled by restoring a software state; recovery must deal with its remaining consequences.
The architectural separation between learned proposals and the path authorized to admit physical action.
Clearance consumed during pre-brake travel and subsequent braking under the stated motion and plant assumptions.
Elapsed time charged before credible braking begins, measured from the event specified by the stopping claim.
The credible deceleration the loaded plant can deliver under declared traction, actuator, supply, and thermal conditions.
Remaining temperature margin before an actuator or brake must reduce its qualified output or duty; the relevant heat path depends on the mechanism.
The ability of the electrical supply to maintain valid operating voltage during coupled load transients.
Memory-transfer capacity available for the model weights needed by a fresh policy evaluation.
A sequence of future setpoints proposed together so one model evaluation supplies several control steps.
The interval over which observations and assumptions still justify using a proposal; longer output does not extend it.
Time between a physical measurement and the feedback correction it produces in the same control loop; this loop-specific delay consumes phase margin.
A feedback-loop stability margin consumed by delay at the loop crossover frequency; it is distinct from a stopping-distance budget.
An upper bound on permitted execution, blocking, interference, and communication delay under declared assumptions.
The bounded interval for which the permission processor may continue executing an admitted action chunk without renewal.
Exclusive physical control over the paths that can energize actuators; fast proposal generation does not grant it.
The change in visited states and subsequent observations caused by the learned policy executing its own actions.
Growth of closed-loop consequences as early policy errors change later states and expose further errors; recovery behavior can limit that growth.
Examples of corrective actions from off-nominal states, rather than only successful progress along an expert path.
Declared external conditions in which the policy is intended to operate and for which its data and evaluation need coverage.
A point predictor averages distinct valid action modes into a motion that may belong to none of them.
Mismatch between training simulation and the physical plant, including contact, sensing, timing, and actuation.
A versioned learned policy whose training provenance, decoder, interface, and evidence must be bound before evaluation and release.
A trial of the complete controller and plant in which actions determine later observations and the declared outcome is scored.
A statistical limit supported by a finite campaign under its sampling and outcome assumptions; no observed failures is not proof of zero risk.
The physical acquisition time attached to an observation, with the relevant clock-conversion and exposure uncertainty.
Elapsed time from physical capture to the point of use; queueing and transport continue to age the evidence.
A qualified bound on measurement and calibration error used to reduce the clearance credited to a motion.
A dated estimate of physical state formed from prior dynamics and measurements, rather than a replacement for current observation.
The estimator's stated uncertainty under its model and noise assumptions; consistency must be tested against physical residuals.
The point when propagated uncertainty or elapsed time exhausts the margin permitting a cached belief to support action.
An action possibility tied to a physical object, the machine's capabilities, and the conditions required to execute it.
A checkable set of acceptable physical outcomes and constraints that gives the planner a specification to satisfy.
A goal proposal with an expiry and validity conditions that must still hold when motion is planned and admitted.
A time-indexed motion proposal carrying the state, horizon, and conditions needed for execution checks.
Compatibility of a proposed path and timing with the plant's velocity, acceleration, torque, and dynamic limits.
A state-matched, smoothly joined braking continuation that remains available if proposal renewal fails.
States and motions that retain sufficient qualified clearance and braking authority for the declared stopping response.
A mechanism that checks or modifies a proposed control against modeled admissibility constraints, conditional on its plant, sensing, and timing premises.
Remaining allowance for contact force, energy, and response delay when the task intentionally touches the environment.
A separately qualified protective function with a stated integrity claim; an unrated numerical filter does not acquire that claim merely by running above it.
Separation or bounded sharing of memory, supply, clock, reset, and compute resources between proposal and permission paths.
Clock or performance reduction induced by a shared thermal state, which can persist after the workload that caused it stops.
A declared upper execution-time bound for a specified binary and platform; observed maxima can falsify it but do not establish it.
Time consumed while a person perceives, decides, and transfers an intervention into the machine's admitted control path.
An authority-transfer protocol that prevents concurrent writers and requires fresh admission before the new proposer controls motion.
A deliberate disturbance at a specified interface used to challenge a declared protection claim.
The coupled external conditions and internal compute, power, thermal, and actuation states over which a claim is qualified.
A criterion fixed before a trial that distinguishes a valid pass, failure, or invalid test against the stated claim.
An inspectable argument connecting physical safety claims to evidence, assumptions, warrants, and possible defeaters.
A signed binding of the release verdict to configuration identities, limits, evidence records, and conditions enforced at startup and operation.
Ongoing physical and organizational premises whose lapse withdraws a release verdict even without a software change.
A record of who accepted operational and organizational decisions, their evidence, conditions, and revocation responsibilities.
An assigned human role that has enough time, information, and effective authority to intervene as the claim requires.
A difference in detection performance across exposed groups that can delay response and consume their stopping clearance unequally.
Different physical states require different responses but produce identical available observations through the action deadline.
An unresolved premise that remains explicit, with its operating restriction, owner, and missing evidence; recording it does not measure it.
